items.title: Isaiah Morgan Interview, 1958-12-01
items.q: We had Jim Robinson on trombone. And had Jim on bass. We had Johnny Devin on banjo. And we had Lil Roy Even. He's dead. We had him on drums.

ctx.x: And I never did see that man no more.

And he came in. I was talking to John Porter and John Porter told me he was in town a few weeks ago. Some place they played up here somewhere. And John Porter, he went home and passed away. He just had told me, he said his heart was bad anyway. Because we was kidding. He said, now there's Jim, he's making his money. And he's not playing. See, when they played the student watches, Jim had to cut out. He wasn't knowing that.
That was a tuxedo band. Yeah.

items.title: Jim Robinson Interview, 1958-12-10
items.q: Oh, they had, you see, Oyl Fushey, my nephew Sidney Brown, Andrew Morgan, Johnny Dave, Shine, Sam Morgan, Isaiah and myself.

ctx.x: Sam. No, the first band, his brother Isaiah Morgan, but Sam, Sam here, his band, his band, the Magnolia band, he had, well, they had a split, you see. Sam had a stroke and he got sick, well, the band split, you see. And after Sam got out, got well, well, he come with his brother and put the band on the Sam name because he had all the work and everything, you know. He's more famous. Put everything in his hand.
So now you joined Isaiah first.
